column1: # CI budgets (#1437). The only place a number is typed: `ci_budget_report.sh` reads this file
# and compares it with a run's own jobs, and the verdict is its exit status.
# `set_from` is the measurement the number came from, quoted with its run id. A budget without
# one cannot be compared to the number it should be, so it is not a check — the report fails on
# the row rather than on the run.
# The ratchet has two halves, and both are enforced by `ci_budget_report.sh --base <ref>`:
#   · a budget may be **lowered** after a win, freely — that is the point;
#   · a budget may **not be raised** unless `set_from` changes too, which is how a raise names
#     what regressed instead of quietly moving the line;
#   · a row may not be deleted. A removed budget makes a breach invisible, not fixed.
# Every row below was set from run 42229151064 (`ef77fb58`, the last full run of the 29-job
# workflow): wall 43.5 min, 159.4 job-minutes. A matrix stage is priced on its **slowest leg**,
# because that is what a stage costs in wall clock; its runner time is the sum of the legs and
# The epic's targets (#1436) are lower than these numbers on purpose: ≤ 22 min wall, ≤ 70
# job-minutes, ≤ 10 min at p50. Children 2-4 earn them by removing work, and each win lowers a
# row here. Setting the ceiling to a target nobody has measured yet would fail on the first
# push and teach everyone to ignore the file.
